title: Just-in-Time Role Factory and Permission Boundary Generator
creator: Liang Chen
description: Implement a Terraform module that generates parameterized, least-privilege IAM role templates on demand (JIT) and accompanying permission boundaries. The module should support service/principal onboarding, produce opinionated defaults for role names, scoped policies, and a permission boundary generator that can be composed with customer-provided statements. It must include drift-detection hooks and a small test harness to verify policy surface area and S2S onboarding flows in CI.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes inputs for: role_name_prefix, intended_principal_type (serviceAccount|service|user), allowed_actions_list, resource_scopes, permission_boundary_extra_statements
Module emits outputs: role_arn, permission_boundary_arn, role_iam_policy_hash, onboarding_instructions_url
Default policy templates restrict admin-level actions; any wildcard actions must be explicit via a allowlist input
CI job validates that generated policy has <= recommended_action_count and denies any global '*' resource unless explicitly allowed
Module provides a terraform plan-time validator that fails planning if a 'dangerous' action (iam:*) is included without an explicit approval tag
End-to-end test: create role in a sandbox VPC, assume role via short-lived credentials, perform a bounded set of actions and succeed/fail as expected
Documentation and onboarding guide published in Confluence with example usage and upgrade notes
technical_notes: Design: template-driven approach using JSON policy artifacts stored under modules/roles/templates with variables interpolated at apply time
Permission boundaries are created as separate managed policies and attached to roles; boundaries can be referenced by customers or managed by Redwood depending on install_type
Use data.aws_iam_policy_document and local policy merging to avoid string concat; include a policy size guard and semantic linter in CI
Provide optional OIDC-compatible trust policy generator for private deploy agents and for federated service principals
Drift detection implemented via a periodic job that compares role_iam_policy_hash output against live IAM and raises an alert in Datadog via webhook if mismatch
tasks: Draft Terraform module API and examples
Implement template library and interpolation helpers
Add permission boundary creation and attachment logic
Add plan-time safety checks and linter integration
Implement CI test harness (sandbox account workflow)
Add drift detection job + Datadog alerting
Write Confluence onboarding doc and runbook

decisions: Prefer explicit allowlists over deny-lists to minimize surprise behavior
Permission boundaries will be separate managed policies to allow observation and reuse across roles
Drift detection will be an opt-in periodic job to minimize noise during initial rollout
Module will not automatically rotate long-lived credentials; recommend using short-lived tokens or Vault/OIDC as part of onboarding
